title: 📰 AI news · November 21

items.title: AI agents found a security hole in 11 minutes
items.text: Amazon analysed an attack: hackers ran the open-source tool Cairn, which controls several AI agents at once. The agents found an unknown flaw in a medical imaging program and took full control of the server. If you run a bot, a site or an agent, yours gets probed non-stop too. Check which programs in your project are open to the internet and when they were last updated.

items.title: Chase customer data leaked through a vendor
items.text: Qubole, a cloud data company that works with JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard, was hacked. Chase customers' names and emails leaked, Mastercard emails of a small group of cardholders, and Visa says no payment data was affected. If you run a bot or a site, your customers' data also sits with vendors. List the services that can reach your data and close the extra ones.

items.title: Court reveals secret UK order to Apple
items.text: A tribunal ruled that the fact of the order for access to Apple customers' data can be made public. It first covered data worldwide, then was narrowed to British users' data in the encrypted cloud. Apple says it has never built a backdoor.

items.title: Claude helped write down a solution to the Riemann hypothesis
items.text: A mathematician at Anthropic wrote the solution in Lean, a language where a computer checks proofs itself. Several mathematicians confirmed the file passes the check. A Stanford postdoc separately posted a proof written without AI; it has not been checked yet.

items.title: Perplexity released document search models
items.text: The pplx-embed-v2-context models read neighbouring chunks of a document and work with text, images and scans. There are 0.6B and 9B versions, from $0.02 per million tokens.

items.title: Anthropic opened 33% above its offer price
items.text: Trading on Nasdaq began at $111.50 against an offer price of $83. At the opening price the company is worth more than two trillion dollars.

items.title: Google will send AI chips to orbit in 2029
items.text: Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket will carry Project Suncatcher satellites with TPU chips in the first quarter of 2029. Each satellite has roughly the computing capacity of one data center rack.

takeaway: Today's stories are about speed and access: AI agents find holes in minutes, and customer data leaks through vendors. Recommendation: list the services and vendors that can reach your data and close the extra ones.
